channel.title: Victoria University of Wellington Law Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Victoria University of Wellington Law Review (wgtn.ac.nz)

item.title: Vic Uni invites CubaDupa festivalgoers to immersive arts sanctuary | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Ever felt overwhelmed at a festival and needed an escape hatch? This year, Vic Uni is giving you one for CubaDupa—and it’s hiding inside the big red building on Vivian Street.

item.title: After a summer of weather disasters, will Kiwis make climate an election issue? | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: As the country counts down to the general election in November, Sam Crawley looks at what survey data tell us about climate concerns and voting behaviour.

item.title: Job performance reviews
item.description: Research has identified numerous problems with conventional performance appraisals—so why keep using them, ask Danaë Anderson and Jeremy Morrow.

item.title: International student numbers surge at Vic Uni | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington posts major rise in international student enrolments and strong growth in arts, politics, and teaching, as well as higher numbers of Māori and Pasifika students.

item.title: Wool interior lining wins coveted accreditation | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: A University-led accreditation awarded to a natural wool building material highlights the importance of sustainability in the construction industry

item.title: How Wellingtonians learnt to live with flocks of screeching kākā | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: The reintroduction of kākā in Wellington hasn’t always been smooth sailing. But this sassy bird has won the hearts of many residents and forced people to think about the city and its environment, writes Cathy Breed.

item.title: Photography research goes global | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Japanese born academic Dr Mizuho Nishioka now calls Paekākāriki home, but her photographic research reaches worldwide.

item.title: HPV self-test boosts cervical cancer screening ‘across the board’, study confirms | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: New research adds to evidence HPV self-testing increases screening rates.

item.title: Bacterial meningitis is deadly, but can also have long-term effects on survivors, new study shows | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Far from a short-term illness, bacterial meningitis can cause ongoing effects that persist long after patients are discharged from hospital, write Octavia Calder-Dawe and Kate Smith.

item.title: Three alumni successful at Kiwibank New Zealander of the Year Awards | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Three alumni of Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington won their categories at the Kiwibank New Zealander of the Year Awards on Thursday 19 March.

item.title: What the coming El Niño climate pattern means for NZ in a warming world | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Previous El Niño events have caused severe droughts that have cost the economy hundreds of millions of dollars. Jim Salinger looks at what the next one may bring.

item.title: Widening political gap deepens cracks in NZ climate consensus | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: The picture of climate opinion in Aotearoa is of a gap between left and right that is not only wide, but widening, writes Sam Crawley.

item.title: AI specialist wins Critic and Conscience of Society Award | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Leading researcher and commentator on Artificial Intelligence, Dr Andrew Lensen, has been recognised by Universities NZ for his contribution to national debate.

item.title: Public health providers have to obey strict cyber security rules—so should private contractors | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Whether they’re in the private or public sector, organisations that deal with healthcare data should be subject to mandatory security audits, argue Gehan Gunasekara, Ian Welch, and Lisa Patterson.

item.title: Her song features in Ryan Gosling’s hit movie, but Erima Maewa Kaihau was once a star too | News | Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
item.description: Austin Haynes looks at the remarkable woman behind a song in te reo Māori that features on the Project Hail Mary soundtrack.
